summary: The API's input contracts, written as Pydantic models. FastAPI validates every request body against these classes before an endpoint runs, rejecting bad input with a `422` response and normalizing the rest (IP addresses, time zones, whitespace). `EventIn` feeds `POST /events` and the pipeline, while the small models back incident triage (`StatusIn`), the AI analyst (`AskIn`), the Risk Lab (`EvaluateIn`, checked against `rules.SIGNALS`) and the live-traffic switch (`TrafficIn`).

notes.text: Docstring: request bodies only. **Pydantic** models declare each field's type and constraints; FastAPI validates incoming JSON against them and answers with a `422` error listing the problems when it does not fit, so untrusted input never reaches the engine unchecked.
Postponed annotations: Pydantic resolves these string hints when each class is built, which is why `datetime` and `Literal` must be real imports below.
`ipaddress` (standard library) parses and validates IPv4 and IPv6 addresses.
`datetime` for the optional event timestamp, `timedelta` for the allowed clock skew, and `timezone` to convert timestamps to UTC.
`Literal[...]` restricts a field to an exact set of values; Pydantic enforces it and the OpenAPI docs list the allowed options.

Pydantic building blocks: `BaseModel` (the parent of every schema), `ConfigDict` (typed model settings), `Field` (defaults plus constraints such as lengths, patterns and ranges) and `field_validator` (custom code that checks or transforms one field).
Imports the rulebook so `EvaluateIn` can check signal names against the real catalogue.
`utcnow`, the platform clock, for the future-timestamp check.

A sample request body for the generated API docs: a deliberately risky login (new device, five failed attempts, suspicious IP) that scores at least 65 (HIGH) when tried from `/docs`. `203.0.113.45` comes from a block reserved for documentation (RFC 5737), so it can never belong to a real host.
The accepted range for event timestamps, used by the validator below.

`EventIn` is the body of `POST /api/v1/events`. `str_strip_whitespace` trims every text field **before** the length and pattern checks, so a location of only spaces is rejected instead of being stored empty (it used to raise "Unusual location" and even "Impossible travel"). `json_schema_extra` attaches `EXAMPLE_EVENT` as the example request in the interactive docs.

Required customer ID matching the regular expression `^USR-\d+$`: the literal `USR-` followed by one or more digits and nothing else (`^` and `$` anchor the start and end). A value such as `bob` gets a 422.
Required event type, limited to four values; anything else is a 422.

Optional timestamp, `None` by default. Pydantic parses ISO-8601 strings such as `2026-01-01T12:00:00Z` into `datetime`, and when the field is missing `pipeline.normalize` stamps the event with the current UTC time.
Required IP address as a string; the `_valid_ip` validator below checks and normalizes it.
Required location label of 2 to 80 characters; 80 matches the `String(80)` column in `database.py`.
Required device ID: `DEV-` followed by digits.
Optional on purpose: `None` means "let the server decide", and `pipeline.process_event` then derives it from whether the device is already registered to this user.
Failed attempts default to 0; `ge=0, le=100` (greater-or-equal, less-or-equal) rejects negative or absurd counts.
IP reputation, one of three values, defaulting to `clean`.
Optional amount, non-negative and capped at one billion (`1e9`) to reject garbage values.
Optional resource name of at most 80 characters, matching its database column.
Outcome of the action, defaulting to `success`.

A custom validator for `ip_address`. In Pydantic v2 validators are class methods, so `@field_validator` sits on top of `@classmethod`; it runs after the basic type check (the default "after" mode), and whatever it returns becomes the field's value.

After `.strip()` removes stray spaces, `ipaddress.ip_address()` accepts IPv4 or IPv6 and raises `ValueError` for anything else. Converting back with `str()` gives the canonical spelling (`2001:0DB8::0001` becomes `2001:db8::1`), so one address is always stored the same way.

Re-raises with a short message: Pydantic turns a `ValueError` raised inside a validator into a normal 422 error reading "Value error, invalid IP address". `from None` drops the original exception from the traceback chain.
A validator for `timestamp`: it stores naive UTC and rejects times the engine can't reason about. In Pydantic v2 validators are class methods, so `@field_validator` sits on top of `@classmethod`.
A missing timestamp stays `None`; `pipeline.normalize` then stamps the event with the current time.

Converts a timezone-aware timestamp to the project's naive-UTC convention: `astimezone(timezone.utc)` shifts the clock time to UTC and `replace(tzinfo=None)` drops the label. Shifting a year-1 date by an offset overflows, and that now becomes a normal 422 instead of a server error.

The range check. A date before 2000 used to crash the pipeline with a 500 when the correlation window was subtracted from it, and a far-future date stayed the customer's latest event forever: it kept their incident open to every later event and topped every list. Five minutes of leeway allows for clock skew between the client and the server.
Returns the normalized value.
`StatusIn` is the body of `PATCH /api/v1/incidents/{id}`: the new triage status, one of three values (a test checks that `BOGUS` gets a 422).

`AskIn` is the body of `POST /api/v1/ai/ask`: a question of 2 to 500 characters. Two is enough for a greeting such as "hi", which the analyst answers. The upper limit bounds how much text the analyst scans and, when OpenAI is configured, forwards to the language model.

`EvaluateIn` is the body of `POST /api/v1/risk/evaluate` (the Risk Lab): a list of signal names. `default_factory=list` builds a new empty list when the field is omitted (never a shared mutable default), and `max_length=len(rules.SIGNALS)` caps the list at the catalogue's size, currently 11.
Custom validator for `signals`, using the same decorator pattern as above.
Collects every requested name missing from `rules.SIGNALS` (the `in` test checks the dictionary's keys), so the error can list all of them, not just the first.

Rejects the request with a message such as `unknown signal(s): Nope`, which FastAPI returns as a 422. Without this check `rules.what_if` would hit a `KeyError`, which the app's catch-all handler would turn into a 500 error.
Returns the list unchanged when every name is valid.
`TrafficIn` is the body of `POST /api/v1/simulation/traffic`: `{"enabled": true}` starts the live-traffic generator and `false` stops it.
